title: Iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis — ISC, SUF and CIA

nodes.label: Cellular Fe / S supply
nodes.rationale: Note carefully what the cited work does and does not show. Islam 2020 and Vigani 2021 measured iron uptake and Fe-S interplay under altered field conditions — nutritional physiology. Neither measured cluster assembly. This entity is T2 because the field effect is demonstrated for the process it names; the assembly entities above remain T3 because that evidence does not reach them.

evidence.claim: The geomagnetic field contributes to efficient iron uptake in Arabidopsis; reducing it to near-null affects root metal reductase activity.
Geomagnetic-field-dependent modulation of iron-sulfur interplay in Arabidopsis, most pronounced under combined Fe and S deficiency.
Reduction of the geomagnetic field to near-null affects Arabidopsis root mineral nutrition.

nodes.label: Scaffold ISU1 (ISC)
nodes.rationale: Holds a transient, solvent-exposed [2Fe-2S] cluster whose assembly involves iron redox chemistry and sulfide transfer. A nascent cluster on a scaffold is more exposed and shorter-lived than a mature one buried in a protein, which makes it a more credible point of perturbation than the finished product.
nodes.caveat: Entirely untested. No experiment has measured scaffold occupancy or transfer rate under any magnetic field condition.

evidence.claim: Frataxin is localised to both chloroplast and mitochondrion and is involved in chloroplast Fe-S protein function in Arabidopsis.

nodes.label: Transfer machinery (HSCB, GRXS15)
nodes.rationale: GRXS15 binds a bridging [2Fe-2S] cluster in its dimeric form, so the cluster is genuinely in transit and solvent-accessible here rather than buried.

nodes.label: NFU carriers (NFU4, NFU5)
nodes.rationale: Transiently hold clusters destined for aconitase, succinate dehydrogenase and lipoyl synthase — precisely the QBM-01/QBM-05 nodes the review nominates. If assembly were field-sensitive, this is the step that would show it first.

evidence.claim: Cytosolic Fe/S protein biogenesis depends on export of a sulfur-containing intermediate from the mitochondrion.

nodes.label: SUF system (plastid assembly)
nodes.rationale: Builds every cluster in the chloroplast, including PSI's FX/FA/FB and ferredoxin's [2Fe-2S]. It is the single upstream dependency of QBM-02's strongest nodes.

nodes.label: Plastid cluster carriers (CnfU, HCF101)
nodes.rationale: The review names CnfU explicitly: Yabe et al. showed the chloroplastic NifU-like protein acts as a scaffold and is required for photosystem I biogenesis, which makes it the direct upstream dependency of QBO:PSI_FES.

evidence.claim: The chloroplastic NifU-like protein CnfU can act as an Fe-S cluster scaffold and is required for biogenesis of ferredoxin and photosystem I.

nodes.label: CIA system (cytosolic assembly)
nodes.rationale: The reason this map matters beyond bioenergetics: CIA clients include the enzymes of DNA replication and repair, so an assembly defect reaches genome maintenance, not just ATP supply.

nodes.label: Fe/S client proteins
nodes.rationale: Collected here so the map can show, in one edge, that a single assembly defect reaches respiration, photosynthesis, the TCA cycle, nitrogen and sulfur assimilation and DNA replication simultaneously. That breadth is the review's argument for why Fe/S biology deserves attention ahead of cryptochrome.
